title: Die Brosamen auf dem Tisch
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 190. Text from Wikisource („Die Brosamen auf dem Tisch (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly. This tale is in Swiss German (Alemannic) dialect; the glossary gives the High German equivalent for each dialect form.
about: A barnyard scene in a few lines of Swiss dialect: a rooster talks his hens into hopping up onto the table to peck crumbs while the mistress of the house is out, promising there is nothing to fear. She comes home early and beats them for it, and the hens' bitter “didn't we tell you so” is met only with the rooster's shrug and a laugh. It is barely a fable, more a joke about who pays for whose bad advice.

sentences.t: Der Güggel het einisch zue sine Hüendlene gseit „chömmet weidli i dStuben ufe goh Brotbrösmele zämmebicke ufem Tisch: euse Frau isch ußgange goh ne Visite mache.“
sentences.l: The cock has once to his little-hens said “come quickly up into the parlour to peck-together bread-crumbs on the table: our mistress has gone out to pay a visit.”
sentences.i: The cock said one day to his hens: “Come along smartly up into the parlour and peck up the bread-crumbs on the table — our mistress has gone out to pay a call.”
sentences.n: Like KHM 167, this tale is printed entirely in Swiss German (Alemannic), and the glossary gives the High German equivalent for every form. Güggel = Gockel, the cock; einisch = einmal, zue = zu, sine = seinen, Hüendlene = Hühnlein, gseit = gesagt, chömmet = kommt, weidli = flink, smartly; ufem = auf dem, euse = unsere, ußgange = ausgegangen. The article d’ is printed onto its noun throughout — dStuben, dFrau, dHüendli. goh with a following infinitive is the Alemannic way of saying “go and do something”, and stands here for High German um … zu.

sentences.t: Do säge do dHüendli „nei nei, mer chömme nit: weist dFrau balget amme mit is.“
sentences.l: Then say the little-hens then “no no, we come not: you know, the mistress scolds every time with us.”
sentences.i: Then the hens said: “No, no, we are not coming — you know the mistress is always scolding us.”
sentences.n: säge = sagen, not die Säge, a saw; nei = nein, mer = wir, not mehr; chömme = kommen, nit = nicht, weist = weißt (du), balget = balgt, scolds; is = uns. amme is a Swiss particle of habit, roughly jeweils or immer wieder — every time, always; its exact force is hard to pin down and the rendering here is the likeliest of several.

sentences.t: Do seit der Güggel „se weiß jo nüt dervo, chömmet er numme: se git is doch au nie nit guets.“
sentences.l: Then says the cock “she knows indeed nothing of it, come you only: she gives us after all also never nothing good.”
sentences.i: Then the cock said: “She knows nothing about it — just come along: she never gives us anything good either.”
sentences.n: seit = sagt, not seit, since; se = sie, jo = ja, nüt = nichts, dervo = davon, numme = nur, not genommen; git = gibt, au = auch. weiß here is the verb wissen, knows, not the colour. chömmet er = kommt ihr — that er is the second person plural pronoun leaning back on the verb, not er, he. nie nit guets piles negative on negative, as the dialect regularly does: never anything good at all.

sentences.t: Do säge dHüendli wider „nei nei, sisch uß und verby, mer gönd nit ufe.“
sentences.l: Then say the little-hens again “no no, it is out and over, we go not up.”
sentences.i: Then the hens said again: “No, no, that is all over and done with, we are not going up.”
sentences.n: wider = wieder, again, not wider, against; sisch = s isch = es ist, uß = aus, verby = vorbei — uß und verby is a set phrase, over and done with; gönd = gehen, ufe = hinauf.

sentences.t: Aber der Güggel het ene kei ruei glo, bis se endlig gange sind und ufe Tisch, und do Brotbrösmeli zämme gläse hend in aller Strenge.
sentences.l: But the cock has them no rest let, until they at last gone are and onto the table, and there bread-crumbs together picked have in all eagerness.
sentences.i: But the cock gave them no peace, until at last they went, and up onto the table, and there picked up the bread-crumbs with a will.
sentences.n: ene = ihnen, not eine; ruei = Ruhe, glo = gelassen, endlig = endlich, gange = gegangen, not der Gang, a passage; hend = haben, zämme gläse = zusammen gelesen, from auflesen, to pick up. bis se … gange sind und ufe Tisch leaves the verb out the second time: they went, and [went] up onto the table. in aller Strenge is the one genuinely doubtful phrase here: Swiss Strengi is effort, hard going, so “with all their might”, but that is a reading and not a certainty.

sentences.t: Do chunt justement dFrau derzue und nimmt gschwind e Stäcke und steubt se abe und regiert gar grüseli mit ene.
sentences.l: Then comes just then the mistress upon them and takes quickly a stick and dusts them down and rules quite horribly with them.
sentences.i: Just then the mistress came upon them, snatched up a stick, drove them down off the table and dealt with them dreadfully.
sentences.n: justement is the French justement, just then, long at home in Swiss speech; derzue = dazu, from dazukommen, to come upon a scene; gschwind = geschwind, e Stäcke = einen Stecken, a stick; steubt … abe = stäubt hinab, drives them down in a cloud. regiert here is not “governs” but goes at them, deals with them; gar grüseli = ganz gräulich, horribly, grüselig being the Swiss all-purpose intensifier.

sentences.t: Und wo se do vor em hus unde gsi sind, so säge do dHüendli zum Güggel „gse gse gse gse gse gse gsehst aber?“
sentences.l: And when they there before the house below been are, so say then the little-hens to the cock “see see see see see see — do you see, though?”
sentences.i: And when they were down in front of the house again, the hens said to the cock: “See, see, see, see, see, see — do you see now?”
sentences.n: wo = als, when: Alemannic uses wo where High German has als or wenn, and it is not wo, where. em = dem, hus = Haus, unde = unten, gsi sind = gewesen sind. The six-fold gse is the hens’ cackling and at the same time the front of gsehst, siehst du — the bird noise turns into the question, and no English spelling can do both at once. aber closing a question is a flavouring word: now do you see?

sentences.t: Do het der Güggel glachet und numme gseit „ha ha han is nit gwüßt?“ do händ se chönne goh.
sentences.l: Then has the cock laughed and only said “ha ha, have I it not known?” then have they been-able to go.
sentences.i: Then the cock laughed and only said: “Ha, ha — did I not know it?” and then they were free to go.
sentences.n: glachet = gelacht, numme = nur again, gseit = gesagt, gwüßt = gewusst. ha ha is the cock’s laugh and at the same time the front of han, habe — the same trick the hens played with gse gse gse running into gsehst; han is = hab ich’s, so is stands for es here and for uns in the middle of the tale. händ se chönne goh is the southern double infinitive, haben sie gehen können. The cock has won the argument, and the tale simply stops.

glossary.amme: jeweils, immer wieder — every time, always (a Swiss German (Alemannic) particle of habit; not die Amme, a wet-nurse)
glossary.au: auch — also, too (Swiss German (Alemannic); not the cry ‘ow’)
glossary.do: da, dort; dann — there; then (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.e: ein; in — a, an; also in (‘e Stäcke’ = einen Stecken; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.ene: ihnen — (to) them (Swiss German (Alemannic); not eine, a)
glossary.er: ihr — you (2nd pl., leaning back on the verb: ‘chömmet er’ = kommt ihr; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.frau: die Frau — the woman of the house, the mistress (‘euse Frau’ = unsere Frau, the farm-wife the hens belong to)
glossary.gange: gehen — gone (past participle, gegangen; Swiss German (Alemannic); not der Gang, a passage)
glossary.gar: gar — quite, thoroughly (an intensifier: ‘gar grüseli’ = ganz gräulich)
glossary.goh: gehen — to go (infinitive; with a following infinitive it means ‘go and do’: ‘goh ne Visite mache’ = um einen Besuch zu machen; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.ha: haben — the front of han, habe (‘ha ha han is nit gwüßt’ = hab ich’s nicht gewusst), and at the same time the cock’s laugh — the same trick as the hens’ gse running into gsehst (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.han: haben — have (1st sg. present, habe: ‘han is nit gwüßt’ = hab ich’s nicht gewusst; also the dialect infinitive; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.het: haben — has (3rd sg. present, hat; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.händ: haben — have (3rd pl. present, haben; Swiss German (Alemannic); not das Händ, hands)
glossary.i: in; ich — in (‘i dStuben ufe’ = in die Stube hinauf); also ich, I (Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.is: uns; es — us (‘mit is’ = mit uns); also es, it (‘han is’ = hab ich’s) (Swiss German (Alemannic); not a form of sein)
glossary.isch: sein — is (3rd sg. present, ist; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.jo: ja — indeed, you know (a flavouring particle; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.mache: machen — to make, to pay (infinitive; ‘ne Visite mache’ = einen Besuch machen)
glossary.mer: wir — we (Swiss German (Alemannic); not mehr, more)
glossary.ne: ein, eine — a, an (reduced; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.numme: nur — only, just (Swiss German (Alemannic); not genommen)
glossary.seit: sagen — says (3rd sg. present, sagt; Swiss German (Alemannic); not seit, since)
glossary.sine: seine — his (dat. pl. sinen; Swiss German (Alemannic))
glossary.säge: sagen — say (3rd pl. present, sagen; Swiss German (Alemannic); not die Säge, a saw)
glossary.ufe: hinauf; auf den — up, upwards (‘i dStuben ufe’ = in die Stube hinauf); also uf with the article (‘ufe Tisch’ = auf den Tisch, onto the table); Swiss German (Alemannic)
glossary.weiß: wissen — knows (3rd sg. present, weiß; not weiß, white)
glossary.wider: wieder — again (Swiss German (Alemannic) spelling; not wider, against)
glossary.wo: als, wenn — when (Swiss German (Alemannic) uses wo where High German has als or wenn; not wo, where)
glossary.zue: zu — to, toward; also the particle of zumachen and zugehen (Swiss German (Alemannic))
